subject: infra.connect
name: Cross-border frequency coordination protocol
position_end: Preferential frequencies for operators, interference-prevention mechanisms and 15 km coordination zones either side of the borders with three neighbours
note: signed alongside a separate free-roaming agreement

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital planning observatory
position_start: Recommended by a 2019 master plan, with ministry work to make it operational since 2023
position_end: A live geospatial platform on eight functional objectives covering network mapping, infrastructure sharing and duplicate-investment reduction, built to international mapping recommendations
note: the minister conceded primary-data quality and availability as the standing problem

subject: infra.connect
name: Domain-name security extensions
position_start: Not deployed
position_end: Cryptographic signing live on the country-code domain's records
sources: 2025-12-09 Burkina Faso Targets Online Trust with New Internet Security Measures (DNSSEC)

subject: infra.connect
name: Fibre and video-surveillance project
position_start: Under construction since July 2021 on a 54-month schedule
position_end: 650 km of backbone plus 150 km of city links, 900 surveillance cameras and 300 video-surveillance sites, on a Chinese concessional loan of RMB 560m
note: the two held records disagree on completion

subject: infra.connect
name: Interconnection catalogue 2026 to 2028
milestone: Published March 2026, revising the call-termination tariff framework
position_end: In force, with call-termination tariffs revised
note: known only through an operator's half-year filing; the catalogue itself is not held

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet exchange point
milestone: Peak capacity raised to 6 Gbit/s under peering support
position_start: Operating since June 2015 at a 6 Gbit/s peak, keeping local traffic flowing through subsea cuts
position_end: Operating at a 6 Gbit/s peak with local latency of 15 to 20 milliseconds against over 300 before peering
sources: 2026-05-25 Local Infrastructure Lower Costs How Peering Is Moving the Needle on Internet Affordability|2025-04-11 Local Businesses Benefit from Burkina Faso's Internet Development (BFIX)
note: no capacity update since May 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: National address-protocol migration roadmap
milestone: Operators and the regulator again call for a roadmap with a timetable
position_end: No adopted national plan or calendar on file, with individual operators migrating on their own schedules
note: a regulator or ministry decision adopting a dated migration plan would settle it

subject: infra.connect
name: National fibre network, deployed length
milestone: Reported in the ministry's 2026 work-plan presentation
position_end: More than 11,292 km deployed, with 270 km more programmed for 2026
note: no earlier cumulative figure on file, so the increment is not derivable

subject: infra.connect
name: National telecommunications backbone, first phase
position_start: 307 km in service at 1,600 Gbit/s
position_end: 307 km in service at 1,600 Gbit/s, the first phase of a stated EUR 175m and 5,740 km programme, with no phase-two status on file
note: financed by a Chinese buyer's credit after a European bank withdrew in 2019

subject: infra.connect
name: New public-administration network
milestone: Architecture finalised, pre-selected suppliers' bids under evaluation
position_start: Network reinforcement and further interconnection named as a priority, with 38 structures interconnected in the first half of 2025
position_end: Architecture of the replacement network complete and equipment procurement in evaluation, with the existing network operating since 2007 and 88 to 100 further buildings connected in 2025
note: the 2025 building count is given as 88 in one source and about 100 in two others

subject: infra.connect
name: Operator site-build commitments
milestone: Ministry follow-up meeting on operator commitments
position_start: 800 new sites planned for 2025 across the fund and the acceleration project, tender in progress
position_end: 2025 commitments delivered in full at 200, 200 and 150 sites across the three operators; for 2026 one operator is at about half of 100 planned and another has five live, twenty installing and 125 in build
note: the 800 planned and the 550 committed-and-delivered are never reconciled in any held source

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite market authorisation
milestone: The minister says she hopes to rule soon on admitting the operator
position_start: No authorisation; the regulator declared terminal sales irregular under the 2008 telecommunications law
position_end: Still unlicensed, with ministry negotiations reported advancing and a decision pending
note: the operator's own continental map still listed the country as available from 2026 without a licence

subject: infra.connect
name: Universal access and service fund
milestone: Role restated at a regulator workshop, 29 June to 2 July 2026
position_start: Financing 500 of the 800 telecom sites planned for 2025, plus 50 more as zones cleared
position_end: Co-financing half the state's FCFA 37.5bn white-zone contribution, levied at 2% of operator turnover
note: no fund account published for any year from 2024 to 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: White-zone connectivity programme, first tranche
milestone: Service orders signed and equipment ordered 2026-04-04
position_start: Tender dossier for 750 localities finalised, project not yet launched
position_end: Most localities identified, service orders signed and equipment on order, with delivery targeted before end-2026
note: officially launched in September 2025, after the window opened

subject: infra.connect
name: White-zone connectivity programme, second tranche
milestone: Announced for 2027 at a working session 2026-04-04
position_start: Not announced
position_end: A second lot of 750 localities announced for 2027, with no separate financing line stated
note: the zero-white-zone-by-2027 framing sits against a 2030 full-coverage horizon for about 2,000 zones

subject: infra.connect
name: Wholesale price on the national fibre backbone
position_start: About 90 million FCFA a month for a 10 Gb service (2023)
position_end: About 35 million FCFA a month for a 10 Gb service (2026), on the operating company's own account of three years running the state-built 3,000 km backbone
note: the figures are the operating company director general's own in an interview; no published tariff schedule is held, and the 3,000 km here does not reconcile with the 307 km first phase and 5,740 km programme the base carries elsewhere

subject: infra.store
name: Data repatriation programme
milestone: 120 externally hosted public platforms inventoried, migration begun
position_start: Not announced; the twelve programmes including this one were unveiled in August 2025
position_end: A localisation doctrine in force with 120 platforms inventoried, migration into the two national data centres begun and completion targeted before end-2026, the inventory expressly still incomplete
note: the minister's own statement that platforms may still be missing is the half that qualifies the count

subject: infra.store
name: Domestic commercial hosting provider
position_start: Did not exist; no wholly domestic commercial hosting provider on record
position_end: Operating with more than 600 domain names, more than 196 web hostings and 98% availability at launch, offering services from domain registration through virtual and dedicated servers to colocation
note: capacity, tier, certification and continuity are unstated, and the wholly-local claim is unverified

subject: infra.store
name: Government cloud
position_start: Not in service; its first datacentres were still under construction
position_end: In operation, its first two modular datacentres inaugurated at Ouagadougou under the zero-data-abroad programme to host, operate and secure all public data and to repatriate data still stored outside the national territory, with no capacity, operator or cost published by the government
note: its facilities are the two modular data centres carried as a separate row; the government's own statement publishes no figure of any kind

subject: infra.store
name: Government mini data centres
position_start: Under construction, with cost then given as over FCFA 15bn
position_end: In operation at about 3,000 terabytes combined, ten times the prior capacity, with more than 7,000 virtual machines at 100 to 300 per ministry, at FCFA 16bn and run by national teams
note: projected savings are stated two ways, about FCFA 30bn over five years and 85 to 95bn over ten

subject: infra.store
name: National big data centre
milestone: Announced for 2028 alongside the mini data centres
position_start: Not announced
position_end: Announced for 2028 to repatriate public and private data, with no cost, siting, tier or procurement on record
note: the mini data centres are explicitly framed as the interim step to it

subject: infra.store
name: Prime-ministerial circular requiring national hosting
position_end: In force and applied when hosting requests are assessed, since local hosting does not appear explicitly in the platforms decree
note: neither the circular's date, number nor text is held

subject: infra.energy
name: Energy supply for rural telecom sites
milestone: No named programme, budget line or target on file
position_end: Power is repeatedly named as a structural constraint on white-zone towers and the ministry says it is improving access to energy for sites, but nothing names an instrument
note: a fund or project document specifying site powering would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Critical-infrastructure classification decree
position_start: The 2024 information-systems security law in force with no identification, classification or mapping machinery
position_end: Decree adopted, defining critical-infrastructure bodies as any entity housing installations indispensable to society's vital functions, expressly spanning energy, water, health, telecommunications and finance
note: adopted at the same sitting as the mass biometric-enrolment decree it will have to cover

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber agency appropriation
position_start: FCFA 498,036,000 appropriated for 2025
position_end: FCFA 489,236,000 appropriated for 2026, against 444,200,000 in 2024
note: the 2024 operations-centre licence and public-address lines do not survive the agency's move between ministry sections

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Digital infrastructure supervision centre
milestone: Site inspected by the digital transition minister 2026-08-05
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A five-storey building under construction at FCFA 3.048bn, delivery scheduled for October 2026, to supervise the national backbone, secure cyberspace, manage state data centres and maintain critical infrastructure. At a ministerial site visit on 2026-08-05 the technical managers put physical execution across this worksite and the first Maison du citoyen together at about 20%, with the minister asking contractors to hold the pace
note: the August account names the build the Centre d’opération du Réseau Backbone national and gives it the same supervisory function; the base does not state in terms that the two names are one building. The 20% figure is a combined rate for two worksites, not this one alone

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National computer emergency response team
milestone: No appropriation found across the 2024, 2025 and 2026 volumes
position_end: No creating instrument, no named operator and no budget line on file, while a private firm sells set-up services into the market
note: a decree creating a national team, or an agency line naming one, would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Regional incident response centre
milestone: Named as a 2026 ambition at a ministry meeting
position_start: Not announced
position_end: Announced as an ambition for the regional confederation, with no host, financing or timetable stated
note: sits alongside a stated intention to pool digital infrastructure across the confederation

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Reported cybercrime complaints and losses
position_start: 3,028 complaints and 1.108 billion FCFA of losses (2022)
position_end: 6,367 complaints and 1.872 billion FCFA of losses (2025)
note: the cybercrime unit BCLCC's own figures, cited at a communications-council digital-security workshop for journalists and web activists held 27-29 July 2026 under law n°014-2024/ALT on information-systems security; complaints have more than doubled since 2022 and losses risen about 69%, but nothing states whether reporting propensity, unit capacity or the offence itself is what grew, and no clearance or prosecution figure accompanies them

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Security audit and auditor accreditation decree
position_start: The law asserted an accreditation duty for auditors with no procedure attached
position_end: Conditions for periodic audits fixed, and accreditation of auditors vested in the national cyberspace control body
note: the accrediting body is named by function, not by institution

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Security-product approval and homologation regime
status: Implemented, approval conditions not on record
milestone: Provided by articles 7 and 9 of the security law of 2024-07-09
position_start: In force by statute, with no implementing regulation on record
position_end: The same, with the decrees of 30 July 2026 fixing audit and auditor accreditation but not the conditions for technical approval or homologation, which the law leaves to regulation
note: importing or selling information-security hardware or software without technical approval carries a fine of FCFA 2m to 100m, at least doubled on repetition

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Electronic travel form
position_start: Did not exist; airport embarkation and disembarkation forms were completed on paper
position_end: Forms filled online, with the border-police director stating that centralised data opens intelligence uses including movement analysis, anomaly detection and risk profiling
note: no retention rule or access control is stated in either account

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National interoperability framework
position_end: Article 7 of the 2024 platform decree leaves it to be adopted by a prime-ministerial order and article 6 conditions go-live on conformity with it, and no held source states its content, publisher, version or status
note: a prime-ministerial order adopting it would settle it, and this is the central missing object of the exchange layer

subject: dpi.id
name: Regional biometric identity card
milestone: Launched with the head of state's own enrolment, December 2025
position_start: Harmonised regional specifications validated by three security ministers in November 2024, with the older card still in issue
position_end: A fifth-generation national card in mass production since January 2026, issuable from age five and required from thirteen, at FCFA 3,500 with ten-year validity, carrying both national and confederal marks and adopted by a second member state in March 2026
note: no enrolment or issuance total has ever been published

subject: dpi.id
name: Unique electronic identifier
milestone: Enrolment decree adopted by the Council of Ministers 2026-07-30
position_start: A 2024 framework law in force with regional awareness workshops running, no vendor and no enrolment
position_end: Vendor recruited and a decree organising mass registration through national, regional, provincial and communal committees run entirely by public structures so that fingerprint and iris data stay sovereign, with mass enrolment targeted before end-2026
note: the 2025 tender failed; the decree states no enrolment target, budget or supervisory authority, and its gazetted text is not held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Certified electronic invoice
position_start: A 2017 paper standard was the traceability instrument; no electronic certified invoice existed
position_end: A certified electronic invoice in operation, with control modules for firms already running invoicing software and invoicing units for those that do not
note: the held source states no mandatory date and no adoption figure

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic-money accounts
milestone: Reported in the central bank's 2024 digital financial services report
position_end: 9.53% of the union-wide 248 million electronic-money accounts opened at end-2024, fourth of the eight member states, with the national treasury one of only two treasuries among the 69 issuing initiatives
note: the report publishes the country share, not a national account total

subject: dpi.pay
name: National payments platform
milestone: Became the collection rail for automated traffic fines 2026-08-01
position_start: Government payments by application, web and short code, covering stamp duty, taxes and duties
position_end: The same, plus payment links for automated traffic fines, with vehicle immobilisation for non-payment within a month
sources: 2026-08-01-burkina-e-verbalisation-1099-infractions-en-12-heures|2026-07-30-burkina-faso-smart-traffic-cameras-ouagadougou|2025-01-30 Burkina Faso launches Faso Arzeka digital payment platform
note: the first case on file of a domestic payment rail carrying a coercive state obligation

subject: dpi.pay
name: Regional instant-payment rail
position_start: A real-condition test phase running, with a union launch announced for September 2025
position_end: Live, with nine domestic institutions authorised by February 2026 and 80 institutions connected union-wide by June 2026, connection deadlines pushed to September 2026 for banks and payment institutions and June 2027 for microfinance
note: the deadline extension is a union-wide decision, not a domestic one

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registration platform
milestone: Thirty communes holding fully digitised registers at end-2025
position_start: 3,391,907 civil-status acts digitised across 54 communes and 145,655 birth certificates issued in 2024
position_end: Thirty communes hold fully digitised registers, and 121,000 civil-status acts were issued to internally displaced people in 2025 against a 65,000 target
note: the two ends count different things, so no rate of progress can be derived

subject: dpi.registry
name: Estate-agency register
milestone: Launched 2026-07-21 under an April 2026 interministerial order
position_start: Did not exist; brokering private residential leases required no licence and no register
position_end: A compulsory national card applied for and tracked wholly online, with a legally recognised virtual card issued on validation and a register the public can query, and commissions capped
note: no count of cards issued or applications received

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land and cadastre platform
milestone: Given statutory footing by an October 2025 law and a March 2026 decree
position_start: Online issue of land-occupation titles since March 2025, with a cadastral extract in one day and a definitive title in sixty
position_end: The same service, now the operating layer of a reformed land regime, with physical files no longer circulating between administrations and falsified titles rejected by the system
note: no figure for titles or extracts actually issued through the platform is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Single social register
position_end: 362,698 households and 2,217,518 people, of whom 1,191,859 women, across 99 communes in ten regions, with about fifty further communes prepared for 2026
note: stated to interoperate with the unique identifier to prevent duplicates

subject: dpi.mis
name: Customs system
milestone: Advanced test phase, production described as imminent
position_start: Procurement of an intelligent customs solution authorised at FCFA 3.313bn, entirely state-budget financed, nothing built
position_end: The system in advanced testing with production imminent
note: no go-live date stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Pension acts platform
milestone: Announced as the completion of the pension programme
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Announced as the platform that will join the pension fund, the civil-service directorate and the budget directorate on a single pension file
note: no date, budget, vendor or scope stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Solidarity platform
position_start: Did not exist; vulnerability alerts were reported late and information dispersed across actors
position_end: Assistance requests and tracking, complaint handling, solidarity appeals, financial contributions and statistical monitoring for social policy
note: no user, case or contribution figure published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Administrative procedures live online
milestone: Reported at the 2025 objectives review, February 2026
position_end: 146 procedures operational out of 272 platforms initiated since the 2023 assises, with 69 new platforms built or started in 2025 and more than 270 procedures still in digitisation
note: the base held no procedure count at the window's opening

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Automated traffic enforcement
milestone: Went live at midnight on 2026-08-01 after a pilot from April 2026
position_start: Did not exist; a 2023 system allowed digital payment of fines an officer had written
position_end: Live in the capital for four offences, with automated plate reading, interconnection to the vehicle database and the payments rail, a national supervision centre, and vehicle immobilisation for non-payment within a month
note: neither account reports a legal basis, retention rule or data-protection authorisation

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Central electronic-services portal
position_start: Did not exist; procedures sat on separate ministry platforms with no authoritative index
position_end: 1,672 information sheets, 95 dematerialised procedures and 183 public institutions on a single gateway, launched partly to counter fraudulent administrative websites, with a parallel citizen-petition platform
note: its 95 procedures do not reconcile with the ministry's own count of 146 live procedures at end-2025

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Certificates issued online
milestone: Reported at a national forum on the digitalisation of justice
position_end: Over 600,000 criminal-record certificates and nearly 70,000 nationality certificates issued through justice-ministry platforms, plus about 2,000 documents from a trade-register service opened in February 2026
note: set against internet access of 72% urban and 27% rural

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Diplomatic and consular service platforms
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Three launched: a diaspora registration and consular-appointment portal, an E-Protocole system for diplomatic cards, and a consolidated site for the ministry and its 52 missions
note: launched by the foreign affairs ministry; no user target, diaspora population figure, cost or supplier is published, and nothing states whether the consular services previously required attendance in person

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-AGRÉMENT-MS health portal
position_start: Did not exist; health-establishment authorisation and partnership-convention procedures required in-person visits between services
position_end: In operation, taking online applications to open and operate private health establishments and for partnership conventions between the ministry and NGOs, associations and foundations, with applicants able to track a file's progress between services; built jointly with the digital transition ministry. More than 247 applications had been lodged since a soft launch in April 2026, of which 39 were validated at the official launch. No cost or timetable for further procedures is stated
note: the application and validation counts are the ministry's own, given at the launch; the 39 validated of 247 lodged is a completion rate the record does not explain

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Official-travel platform
position_start: Did not exist; official missions ran on a circuit made obligatory by prime-ministerial circular
position_end: All state-funded official travel including air-ticket booking must be processed through the platform, which identifies the most competitive offer automatically
note: locally developed, with no spend, saving or transaction figure published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Pension formalities portal
position_start: Did not exist; pension formalities were handled on paper across three administrations
position_end: Online pension formalities, presented as improving data exchange between the pension fund, the civil-service directorate and the budget directorate rather than as a web front end

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Public platforms hosted abroad
milestone: First inventory disclosed at the Prime Minister's review 2026-07-25
position_end: 120 platforms inventoried, migration into the two national data centres begun and repatriation to finish before end-2026, with the minister stating investigations continue to find platforms not yet listed
note: no count existed before this one, and the inventory is self-declared incomplete

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Trade single window
milestone: Statutes converting the operator into a state company approved 2026-07-23
position_start: The platform operating since February 2016 under a company wholly owned by the chamber of commerce
position_end: The same platform, its operator converted into a state company on the stated ground of improving the governance of strategic digital tools
note: an ownership change to trade infrastructure, not a platform change

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Treasury platforms
position_start: Did not exist; the treasury deposit bank had operated since August 2024 with no online channel
position_end: One platform carries treasury teleprocedures and the other is the treasury bank's round-the-clock online banking, both built in-house and financed under a World Bank project
note: no user or transaction figure for either platform

subject: gov.legislate
name: Enforcement decrees under the 2021 law
position_start: Absent, with the commission pleading for their adoption to the Prime Minister in March 2025
position_end: Still never issued when the commission was superseded in August 2026
note: publication of any implementing decree, or its express abrogation, would settle it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Fast-track procurement decree
position_start: A fast-track procurement route with loose conditions of recourse
position_end: Recourse restricted to national sovereignty, strategic character, grave threat to public order, security or service continuity, and humanitarian consequences of insecurity
note: a rereading required by the revolutionary charter adopted in April 2026; the digital ministry has used this route repeatedly

subject: gov.legislate
name: Headquarters-localisation decree
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Firms above a revenue threshold must build headquarters in-country, with building standards set by revenue band
sources: 2026-02-13 Burkina Faso Orders Large Firms to Build Local Headquarters
note: the built-environment counterpart to data localisation, and it hits the three mobile operators

subject: gov.legislate
name: Information-systems security law
position_start: In force since July 2024, with the auditor-accreditation duty asserted without machinery
position_end: Now carrying a decree identifying, classifying and setting obligations for critical-infrastructure bodies, plus a decree fixing periodic audits and auditor accreditation
note: the mapping instrument lands before the biometric enrolment it will have to cover

subject: gov.legislate
name: Whistleblower protection law
milestone: In preparation by the justice ministry
position_start: Carried by the justice minister, in preparation
position_end: No held source records adoption or any further step in the eighteen months since

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital contribution to the RELANCE 2026-2030 plan
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: Under formulation: the digital transition ministry working out what it contributes to the national plan
note: a ministerial CASEM session on the ministry's contribution to the RELANCE 2026-2030 national plan; the plan text, the digital component, any budget line and any target are all unheld, so what is recorded is that the process is running and not what it will produce

subject: gov.standards
name: Information-systems management procedures manual
position_start: A regulatory duty on every public service for more than twenty years, with no manual in existence
position_end: Validated as a harmonised reference framework for ministerial information-systems directorates, with formal approval by joint ministerial order not recorded as signed
note: signature of the joint order would settle it

subject: gov.standards
name: Public digital platforms decree
milestone: Signed 2024-08-02 as a regularisation, deliberated in Council 2024-05-08
position_start: In force, requiring a prior favourable technical opinion before development or acquisition and a security non-objection before go-live
position_end: The same regime, with three sequential consents and an obligation on the supplier or in-house team to assign the full source code and current documentation before a platform goes into service
sources: 2024-08-02-burkina-decret-plateformes-numeriques-administration-publique|2026-02-19-decret-plateformes-numeriques-publiques|2024-05-13 Burkina Faso Revamps Public Administration with Digital Platform Decree
note: held as an image scan read by OCR; the decree itself says it is issued as a regularisation

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection commission
position_start: An operating authority with no repressive powers, its standing borrowed from a prime-ministerial compliance campaign
position_end: Superseded as data-protection supervisor on the face of the August 2026 votes, never having received the enforcement decrees it asked for in March 2025

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law of 2021
position_start: In force as the operative statute with an annual-reporting duty, and no repressive powers because the implementing decrees were never made
position_end: Still the operative text, since the successor voted in August 2026 is not promulgated, and the decrees were never issued in the five years the law ran

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law of 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Voted with processing without consent prohibited and sanctioned, administrative fines indexed to turnover and scaled by gravity, transfer of sensitive data abroad prohibited, use of personal data for commercial prospecting prohibited without prior consent and enforced by administrative sanctions of the regulator without prejudice to court action, and private video-surveillance devices left lawful but framed where they face the public highway
note: no text, number or gazette reference held; it must clear conformity review before promulgation

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection authority annual report
milestone: Validated in plenary June 2025, not published
position_start: Validated at the authority's sixth plenary session, unpublished
position_end: Still not found published as at 2026-07-25, against the statutory reporting duty, and a press-freedom body recorded that no report was made public for 2024
note: publication on the authority's site would settle it

subject: gov.protect
name: Merged communication and data-protection authority
status: In development, organic law voted awaiting promulgation
position_start: Did not exist; the broadcasting regulator and the data-protection commission were separate
position_end: A single authority merging the broadcasting regulator created in 1995 and the data-protection commission instituted in 2004, with its own rule-making power and staggered renewal of the first college, the state news agency placing the merger under the revised Constitution of 20 January 2026; no commencement, seat or leadership stated
note: nothing on file establishes how its independence, budget or appointment route is secured

subject: gov.protect
name: Non-profit register decree
position_start: A register governed by a 2017 decree with no retention period for the data it holds
position_end: Replaced under a 2024 anti-money-laundering law, fixing for the first time a retention period for the data after dissolution and adding donation declarations and intervention-theme fields
note: a surveillance register acquiring a data lifecycle

subject: gov.discourse
name: Broadcasting regulator
status: Implemented, mandate transferred subject to promulgation
milestone: Communication-regulation mandate inherited by the merged authority
position_start: A standalone regulator of public communication exercising new social-media powers over users with 5,000 or more followers
position_end: Its regulation of public communication passes to the merged authority, putting broadcast-content regulation and data-protection supervision under one college
note: the merger removes the separation that let one act as a check on the other

subject: gov.discourse
name: Organic law on social-media regulation
position_start: Extends regulatory powers to social-media users with at least 5,000 followers, with operationalisation started in 2024
position_end: Same; no held source records any change, and the enforcing body is folded into the merged authority
note: the only social-media-regulation instrument the base holds for this country

subject: include.divides
name: Digital programme for girls and women
position_end: A EUR 2.25m grant from 2021 to 2025, recorded closed, with no evaluation, outturn or beneficiary count in the base
note: the only gender-and-digital finance instrument the base holds for this country, and it has ended

subject: include.divides
name: Real fourth-generation coverage
milestone: Stated by the director-general of electronic communications
position_end: Fell from 53% to 33% on insecurity
note: no held source dates the earlier figure

subject: include.divides
name: Repeated household access survey
position_end: The only survey instrument the base names dates from 2013, and the urban and rural access split has no second reading

subject: include.divides
name: Sahel connectivity project
milestone: A 2021 to 2026 project report published June 2026
position_start: Running, serving more than 3,650 users across two countries including host communities and refugees
position_end: The project report published, with US$1.2m contributed by one European state, a vendor supplying access points and another agency training local teams
note: covers three countries jointly, with no country-only figure in the base

subject: include.divides
name: Urban and rural internet access gap
milestone: Figures presented at a national forum on the digitalisation of justice
position_end: Internet access at about 72% urban against about 27% rural
note: not repeated or disaggregated by gender anywhere in the base

subject: include.access
name: Consumer-protection rules
milestone: Enforceable after a court ruling, announced 2025-12-02
position_start: Adopted in 2023 but suspended and unenforceable
position_end: In force, with main-balance validity extended from 90 to 180 days, promotional credit usable across networks and minimum one-month validity on data bundles; the regulator reports standard mobile-internet prices down 28 to 45%
